title: Punção / infusão subaracnoide
author: Gabriel Magalhães Nunes Guimarães
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.s63ehgn

steps.title: Obtain Informed Consent
steps.instruction: Conduct the informed consent process with the patient or their legal representative.

substeps.instruction: For patients >18 years with intact comprehension: explain the procedure, expected sensations/discomforts, common and uncommon risks, alternatives, and benefits.
Verify patient understanding through simple questions.
Obtain signature on the institution's informed consent form.
For patients <18 years or with altered comprehension: obtain informed consent from the legal representative and provide simplified assent to the patient using comics, drawings, or animations.

steps.title: Perform Risk Assessment
steps.instruction: Screen for potential complications via medical record review, consultation with the requesting physician, patient interview, and physical or complementary examinations.

substeps.instruction: Assess risk of herniation (e.g., intracranial hypertension).
Assess risk of expansive epidural hematoma (e.g., anticoagulant use).
Assess risk of hemodynamic instability (e.g., severe aortic stenosis).
Assess risk of difficult subarachnoid puncture (e.g., obesity, spinal surgery).
Assess risk of contamination (e.g., infection, tattoos, or tumors at the puncture site).

steps.title: Prepare Materials and Equipment
steps.instruction: Gather and verify all necessary sterile supplies within their expiration dates.

substeps.instruction: Select puncture needle: preferably 27G pencil-point, or 25G cutting needle if a difficult puncture is anticipated.
Prepare syringes: one for subarachnoid medication infusion and one for the anesthetic button.
Prepare aspiration/injection needles (preferably 21G or 23G).
Prepare a closed sterile procedure tray.
Prepare closed ampoules of solutions for subarachnoid or anesthetic button infusion.
Prepare closed sterile gauze packages and sterile gloves of appropriate size.
Prepare antiseptic solution (preferably alcoholic chlorhexidine, or 70% alcohol as a second option).

steps.title: Patient and Provider Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the patient and the clinical team for the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Expose the puncture site and surrounding area.
Position the patient sitting up to facilitate the procedure, provided there are no contraindications (e.g., cord prolapse).
Install monitors (oximetry, cardiocopy, non-invasive blood pressure, or invasive blood pressure if required) before starting if there is a significant risk of complication.
Anesthesiologist must wash hands with soap and water, dry them, and don sterile gloves using proper technique.
Assistant opens the first stage of the block tray and provides supplies (alcohol in bowl, gauze, syringes, needles) using a technique that maintains sterility.
Aspirate solutions intended for subarachnoid infusion first, before any other solution, to prevent accidental infusion of incorrect substances.

steps.title: Perform Subarachnoid Puncture
steps.instruction: Execute the puncture and administration/collection process.

substeps.instruction: Perform antisepsis within a 15cm radius of the puncture site.
Allow the antiseptic solution to evaporate spontaneously.
Place a sterile field.
Verify the puncture site using anatomical or ultrasound references.
Administer the anesthetic button at the puncture site.
Introduce the subarachnoid puncture needle.
Confirm cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) reflux.
Collect CSF (if for examination) or infuse planned medications.
Remove the needle at the end of the procedure.

steps.title: Post-Procedure Care
steps.instruction: Manage the patient following the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Position the patient according to the objective of the puncture.
Provide surveillance and monitoring based on patient risks, puncture objectives, and substances infused.
